title: workbench/README.md exceeds Docker Hub's 25,000-byte limit
description:
`workbench/README.md` is 25,069 bytes, 69 bytes over Docker Hub's
25,000-byte limit for repository full descriptions. Every production
build's README push fails as a result:

https://github.com/posit-dev/images-workbench/actions/runs/29355616351/job/87197718403

400 Client Error: Bad Request for url:
https://hub.docker.com/v2/namespaces/posit/repositories/workbench

Introduced in 2ae80a2 ("docs: document PWB_SSSD and sssd disable
options for workbench"), which pushed the file from 24,719 to 25,069
bytes.

Fix: trim the README by 69+ bytes.

title: libnss_pwb symlink is deleted by ldconfig during R install, breaking pwb NSS module in all workbench-session images
description:
## Summary

The `libnss_pwb` NSS module wiring in `workbench-session` images is broken: the dangling multiarch symlink created at build time is deleted by `ldconfig` during the R install step, on every image built since the feature was added (#7b18044). As a result, the "rootless in-session identity resolution" feature has never actually been active in any shipped `workbench-session` image — it silently fails the same way the intended dormant/fallback state does, so it wasn't caught by functional testing.

This was surfaced by `bakery dgoss run --matrix-versions only --latest --image-platform linux/amd64` on the `deps/session-image-packages` branch, which adds a `Standard` variant to `workbench-session`. The existing goss test happened to become meaningful for the first time on that variant.

## Root cause

`workbench-session/template/Containerfile.ubuntu{2204,2404}.jinja2` contains:

```dockerfile
### Enable the pwb NSS module for rootless in-session identity resolution ###
# libnss_pwb.so is delivered at runtime by the workbench-session-init container
# into /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/. Create the (build-time dangling)
# multiarch symlink + nsswitch entries so glibc loads it once that volume is
# populated. Dormant-safe: with no workbench-nss.conf the module returns
# Unavail and resolution falls through to `files`.
RUN case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
      amd64) TRIPLET=x86_64-linux-gnu ;; \
      arm64) TRIPLET=aarch64-linux-gnu ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported arch ${TARGETARCH}"; exit 1 ;; \
    esac && \
    ln -sf /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/libnss_pwb.so \
           "/usr/lib/${TRIPLET}/libnss_pwb.so.2" && \
    ...
```

The symlink target (`/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/libnss_pwb.so`) does not exist at build time — it's meant to be populated by a runtime mount from `workbench-session-init`. Several build steps later, `RUN` install of R (`rstd.io/r-install`) installs a `.deb` via `apt-get install ./r-*.deb`, which triggers `libc-bin`'s `ldconfig` postinst trigger. **`ldconfig` deletes symlinks in the multiarch lib directories whose target does not exist at all** (as opposed to an existing-but-empty target, which it merely warns about). This silently removes `/usr/lib/<triplet>/libnss_pwb.so.2` before the image is even finished building.

I confirmed this two ways:
1. Extracted the built `workbench-session` image layers (`docker save` + tar inspection) and found a `.wh.libnss_pwb.so.2` whiteout entry in the same layer as the R-install `RUN` command, in **both** the Minimal and Standard variants.
2. Isolated repro on bare `ubuntu:24.04`:
   ```bash
   ln -sf /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/libnss_pwb.so /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnss_pwb.so.2
   RUN_UNATTENDED=1 R_VERSION=4.6.1 bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://rstd.io/r-install)"
   ls -la /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnss_pwb.so.2   # No such file or directory
   ```
   Creating an empty placeholder *file* at the target path first (`touch /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/libnss_pwb.so`) before the symlink prevents the deletion — `ldconfig` then only logs `File ... is empty, not checked.` and leaves the symlink in place.

## Why the goss test didn't catch this until now

`workbench-session/matrix/test/goss.yaml` has:
```yaml
"Verify libnss_pwb symlink present current architecture":
  exec: 'dpkg-architecture -qDEB_HOST_MULTIARCH | xargs -I{} test -L "/usr/lib/{}/libnss_pwb.so.2"'
```
`dpkg-architecture` is not installed in the `Minimal` variant, so the left side of the pipe produces no output, `xargs` never invokes `test -L`, and the command exits 0 — the test vacuously passes without checking anything. It only became a real assertion on the new `Standard` variant (which pulls in `dpkg-dev` transitively via one of the added `-dev` packages), where it correctly fails.

## Suggested fix

In the same `RUN` block, create a placeholder regular file at the symlink target before creating the symlink, so `ldconfig` sees an existing (if empty) target instead of a fully dangling one:

```dockerfile
    esac && \
    mkdir -p /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble && \
    touch /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/libnss_pwb.so && \
    ln -sf /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/noble/libnss_pwb.so \
           "/usr/lib/${TRIPLET}/libnss_pwb.so.2" && \
```//jammy" for the 22.04 template.

Separately, the Minimal-variant goss test should be made to actually assert something regardless of whether `dpkg-architecture` is present (e.g. compute the triplet via `uname -m`/a static case statement instead of relying on `dpkg-dev`), so it doesn't silently mask regressions like this one again.

## Affected files

- `workbench-session/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2204.jinja2`
- `workbench-session/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2404.jinja2`
- (rendered) `workbench-session/matrix/Containerfile.ubuntu{2204,2404}.{min,std}`
- `workbench-session/matrix/test/goss.yaml` (+ its template) for the Minimal-variant test gap

title: Help admins understand which image to customize for different purposes
description:
It's a lot to expect an admin to appreciate the interplay between `workbench`, `workbench-session-init`, `workbench-positron-init`, and `workbench-session`.

Provide a quick reference to direct admins to which image to customize for different use cases:

e.g., 
1. To add additional system dependencies or versions of R/Py/Qu: customize `workbench-session` using <links> examples as a guide
2. To update the version of Workbench, update `workbench` and `workbench-session-init` 
3. To change workbench config, customize `workbench`
4. To install a more recent positron version than what ships with `workbench`, use `workbench-positron-init`
5. etc.

description: Analog to https://github.com/posit-dev/images-connect/pull/92. Workbench session images require `libuv1-dev` for `fs` support.

title: Evaluate system package lists for Workbench images
description:
# Summary

The package lists used in this repository are largely lifted from rstudio-docker-products which may not have up-to-date dependencies. We should evaluate our system dependency lists to determine if any packages should be removed, moved between required and optional, or added.

# Methodology

Required packages should include system dependencies that are...

* Required by what is installed into the minimal image
* Not subject to a user's specific environment or opinions (like Python or R versions)

Optional packages should include system dependencies that are...

* Used by nearly all users
* Dependencies of popular R and Python packages
* Used for advanced configurations for subcomponents like authentication
* Required for things to "just work"

title: Vulnerability Scanning and Remediation Before Official Release
description:
**Task**: Before transitioning this product from public preview to official release, perform comprehensive vulnerability scanning and remediation of all CRITICAL and HIGH level vulnerabilities found.

- Run the latest vulnerability scans against all relevant images and dependencies
- Prioritize remediation of all CRITICAL and HIGH findings 
- Document all remediation steps and validate effectiveness
- Confirm no CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities remain (or document and justify any exceptions)
- Indicate readiness for production release after remediation

This is a release-blocking requirement to ensure the security posture of the software.

title: Add CLI text editors to workbench-session image
description:
Original issue: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/issues/873

Currently, it appears that our r-session-complete images don't include any way to edit text on the CLI, no vim or nano. We should add these to images since they are relatively small and cause a poor admin and user experience when trying to verify pod configuration files and other pod specific details. Also some users prefer to do some editing with these files.

title: Add RHEL 10 (UBI) support for workbench-session / workbench-session-init
description:
Phase 3 of the RHEL 10 (UBI) initiative (posit-dev/images-shared#575).

Extends RHEL 10 (UBI) support to the `workbench-session` (R x Python
matrix) and `workbench-session-init` images, once base `workbench`
support (posit-dev/images-workbench#175) lands.

## Notes

Blocked by #175. Also note: `workbench-session-init` already bundles
`rhel8`/`rhel9`/`rhel10` session-launcher binaries for remote compute
targets — that's unrelated to this image's own base OS and shouldn't be
conflated with this work.

title: Add RHEL 10 (UBI) support for workbench (Standard/Minimal)
description:
Phase 2 of the RHEL 10 (UBI) initiative (posit-dev/images-shared#575).

Workbench has no RHEL/UBI support today — this is first-time enablement.
posit-dev/images-package-manager#130 (RHEL 10 UBI support) is the
closest precedent.

## Approach

- Standard and Minimal builds on `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi`,
  amd64 + arm64
- Validate R and Python install and run correctly on RHEL 10 (requires R
  4.6.1+ to avoid the flexiblas-devel issue fixed in
  rstudio/r-builds#329)

## Notes

`posit_product/main.py`'s distro-tag resolver already handles Workbench
generically (`"rhel" + version`) — no code change needed there.

Don't conflate with workbench-session-init's existing `rhel8`/`rhel9`/
`rhel10` goss checks — those validate bundled remote-session-launcher
binaries for compute targets, unrelated to this image's own base OS.

Out of scope: `workbench-session`/`workbench-session-init` (tracked
separately).

title: Remove legacy pre-rootless conditionals from workbench templates
description:
## Summary

The `workbench` Jinja templates independently define a `rootless_support` flag in four places: `Containerfile.ubuntu2204.jinja2`, `Containerfile.ubuntu2404.jinja2`, `startup/supervisord.conf.jinja2`, and `test/goss.yaml.jinja2`.

```
rootless_support = Image.IsDevelopmentVersion
    or (year > 2026)
    or (year == 2026 and month >= 6)
```

Each conditional it guards keeps a pre-rootless code path alive: legacy GID drift handling, root-owned supervisord, the old `/startup/user-provisioning` copy, and non-deterministic UID/GID assignment from before commit d6195b2 reserved UID/GID 999 deterministically.

Every version `bakery.yaml` will add going forward is already past the `2026.06` cutoff (or is a dev build), so the `else`/`not rootless_support` branches are permanently dead for any future template render.

## This is a go-forward-only template change

Templates only affect versions that are explicitly re-rendered with `bakery update files --image-name ... --image-version ...`. Already-released version directories that predate `rootless_support` (`2025.09.2`, `2026.01.2`, `2026.04.0`, `2026.05.1`) are static, already-rendered files. **They are not touched by this change and do not need to be updated or re-rendered** — their legacy GID/user/socket logic stays exactly as it is today.

## Scope

- `workbench/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2204.jinja2`
- `workbench/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2404.jinja2`
- `workbench/template/startup/supervisord.conf.jinja2`
- `workbench/template/test/goss.yaml.jinja2`

## Verification

Re-render the latest active version and confirm the output is byte-identical to what's already committed:

```
bakery update files --image-name '^workbench$' --image-version <latest-version>
git status --short
```

## Follow-up

The `ubuntu-2604` branch (adding Ubuntu 26.04 support, not yet merged) introduces a fourth copy of this same expression in `Containerfile.ubuntu2604.jinja2`. That branch should pick up this cleanup on its next rebase.
